content: {"rules": ["Forecast models consistently overestimate prices, showing upward bias despite negative supply net events.", "Sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish during high auction frequency, triggering downward price corrections.", "Model forecasts lag behind true outcomes by 2–3 days, suggesting delayed reaction to event-driven supply shocks.", "High bearish sentiment correlates with sharp price drops, especially after consecutive auction supply events.", "Price mean-reversion is triggered when sentiment turns negative and supply net is consistently negative.", "Forecast accuracy improves when bullish sentiment outweighs bearish sentiment, even with high event count.", "Model overconfidence in gradual price increases fails during sudden supply shocks, leading to overshoots.", "Price corrections are amplified when sentiment is negative and supply net is large and negative."]}
